hints: Focus on what makes each halogen different, oxidising power, physical state, and how strongly they can reduce sulfuric acid.
Remember that oxidising strength decreases down Group 17, so iodine is still an oxidiser just a weaker one, and volatility falls as London forces get stronger.
Write the equation for $\text{H}_2 + \text{Cl}_2$ in a 1:1 ratio and compare bromide versus iodide as reducing agents toward concentrated sulfuric acid.
walkthrough:
**Check oxidising ability**

All halogens can gain electrons, so all can act as oxidising agents. The power just gets weaker down the group from chlorine to iodine.

Trend: $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2$ as oxidising agents

**Check volatility trend**

Volatility means how easily a liquid or solid turns to vapour. Down the group molecules get bigger, so London forces get stronger.

Result: melting and boiling points rise, so volatility decreases from $\text{Cl}_2$ (gas) to $\text{I}_2$ (solid)

**Check hydrogen plus chlorine reaction**

Hydrogen and chlorine react explosively in sunlight to give hydrogen chloride only.

$$\text{H}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{HCl}$$
With a 1:1 equimolar mixture, both reactants are used up exactly, so only one product forms.

**Check sodium bromide plus concentrated acid**

Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ first makes $\text{HBr}$, then $\text{HBr}$ reduces the acid to $\text{SO}_2$ and is itself oxidised to $\text{Br}_2$. It is not strong enough to reduce sulfur all the way to $\text{H}_2\text{S}$.

$$2\text{HBr} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Br}_2 + \text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$\text{H}_2\text{S}$ is only formed with $\text{NaI}$, because $\text{HI}$ is a stronger reducing agent.

options.A: Incorrect. Iodine can still accept electrons and be reduced to $\text{I}^-$, so it is an oxidising agent. It is just weaker than bromine and chlorine, which is a common trap.
options.B: Incorrect and reversed. Larger molecules down the group have stronger London forces, higher boiling points and lower volatility. Chlorine is a gas, bromine is a volatile liquid, iodine is a solid.
options.C: Correct. The explosive photochemical reaction $\text{H}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{HCl}$ uses up equimolar amounts exactly, giving hydrogen chloride as the sole product.
options.D: Incorrect. With solid $\text{NaBr}$, concentrated sulfuric acid is reduced only to $\text{SO}_2$, with $\text{Br}_2$ formed. $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ forms with $\text{NaI}$ because iodide is a powerful enough reducing agent, bromide is not.
